title: SeqPhase affinity splitter and compact telemetry encoder
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Long-running sequence workloads show phase-locality (repeated token patterns and KV cache hotpaths) which our current batcher treats uniformly. This PR introduces a small runtime shim (SeqPhase affinity splitter) that tags requests with a lightweight phase fingerprint and routes them to device pools optimized for their phase characteristics, reducing cache churn and avoiding cross-phase interference. In parallel, the PR adds a compact telemetry encoder to reduce trace payload sizes from the bench harness and reporting pipeline, lowering upload bandwidth and storage costs for long experiment runs.

Design summary: The change has three parts in one cohesive patch: 1) a splitter component in the workload runner that computes a 64-bit phase hash based on n-gram token windows and recent sequence boundary markers, plus a scoring heuristic to decide affinity buckets; 2) a device-pool policy extension so the runner can express affinity hints (prefer_same_phase / prefer_diverse) to the scheduler; 3) a compact telemetry encoder that packs event streams with delta-encoded timestamps, token-delta compression, and optional zstd-lite compression for large traces. The encoder is pluggable and defaults to no compression for interactive runs.

What I changed (high-level): Added a new workload runner variant (seqphase-runner) and a reporter pipeline stage (compact-telemetry-encoder). Introduced an internal API surface for phase fingerprints and affinity metadata that is intentionally minimal (two fields on the request envelope) to keep compatibility with existing schedulers. Updated the benchmark harness to exercise heterogeneous device pools (GPU/CPU mix) and added golden test vectors for the phase hash to ensure determinism across languages. Updated docs and examples to show how to opt into affinity routing and telemetry compression.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime shim implemented and unit-tested - [x] Integration tests with multi-pool scheduling - [x] Telemetry encoder unit tests and roundtrip verification - [x] Bench runs on small and medium clusters (results attached) - [x] Docs and examples updated - [x] Security and privacy review for fingerprinting heuristic (no user PII used)

Testing and results: I ran the full benchmark suite on a 4-node GPU test cluster and compared baseline runner vs seqphase-runner across three representative workloads (chatty short-turns, long-coherent completions, mixed-burst). Results (median of 10 runs): - Chatty short-turns: p50 latency unchanged, p95 reduced by 12% (less KV cache eviction) - Long-coherent completions: throughput +6% (more stable KV reuse), p95 tail slightly improved - Mixed-burst: p95 reduced by 18%, sustained throughput +9% Telemetry bandwidth: compact encoder reduced average trace payload size by 4.1x and archive storage by ~3.5x for long runs.

Backward compatibility: The affinity hints are optional and ignored by older schedulers. The phase fingerprint algorithm is deterministic and versioned; the runner emits a version field so older consumers can safely ignore it. The telemetry encoder is a reporter option and will not be used unless enabled in pipeline config.

Related work: This complements earlier kernel batching optimizations (see ENG-3119) and the KV cache priming patches. The fingerprint idea was prototyped in an internal spike (ENG-4388) and reviewed by the serving/runtime team.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the deterministic properties of the phase fingerprint, the scheduler API surface (small, intentionally conservative), and the telemetry encoding format (compact but auditable). I included bench artifacts and raw traces in the attached CI artifact for reproducibility.

review_comments: Evan Miller: Nice approach. One concern: have you tried the fingerprint on multilingual prompts? The tokenization boundary behavior can skew windows. Please add a test.

Priya Shah: Added a multilingual test vector (see test_seqphase_fingerprint.py) and documented boundary invariants. The fingerprint uses token IDs not raw chars so it is stable across language inputs with the same tokenizer.
Caroline Wu: Need a short security blurb in docs that explains we do not use PII and that fingerprints are non-reversible. Also add a feature flag so infra can disable affinity at runtime.
Priya Shah: Added the security blurb and a runtime feature flag (BENCH_SEQPHASE_AFFINITY=false). See docs and runner config.
Nikolai Petrov: Perf numbers look promising; can you re-run mixed-burst with larger batch sizes and attach flamegraphs? Also resolve minor lint failures.
Priya Shah: Reran mixed-burst with batch sizes up to 512, attached flamegraphs in CI artifact; fixed linting issues reported by pre-commit.
Evan Miller: Approved after addressing comments.
release_notes: Introduce seqphase affinity routing and optional compact telemetry encoding. Expected improvements: reduced p95 tail on mixed workloads and significantly smaller bench trace archives when compression enabled. Backwards compatible and behind runtime feature flag.
notes: This PR is intended to be non-invasive; enable via bench config. Follow-up work: scheduler-side load balancing heuristics and a small UI in the observability pack to visualize phase buckets.
